public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1034

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1034](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1034)
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*.
  Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
- [MaTa25] Ma, Jie and Tang, Quanyu, *On Erdős problem #1034*.
  [staff.ustc.edu.cn/~jiema/Erdos-1034.pdf](http://staff.ustc.edu.cn/~jiema/Erdos-1034.pdf)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos1034

/--
`JoinedToTwo G T Y` holds when every vertex of `Y` is joined to at least two (distinct)
vertices of `T`.
-/
def JoinedToTwo {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (T Y : Finset V) : Prop :=
  ∀ y ∈ Y, ∃ u ∈ T, ∃ v ∈ T, u ≠ v ∧ G.Adj y u ∧ G.Adj y v

/--
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with $>n^2/4$ many edges. Must there be a triangle $T$ in $G$
and vertices $y_1,\ldots,y_t$, where $t>(\frac{1}{2}-o(1))n$, such that every $y_i$ is joined to
at least two vertices of $T$?

A conjecture of Erdős and Faudree; a stronger version of [905].

This has been solved in the negative by Ma and Tang [MaTa25], who construct a graph with $n$
vertices and $>n^2/4$ edges in which every triangle has at most $(2-(5/2)^{1/2}+o(1))n$ vertices
adjacent to at least two of its vertices (note that $2-(5/2)^{1/2}\approx 0.4189$).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1034.lean"]
theorem erdos_1034 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 4 < (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) →
        ∃ T : Finset (Fin n), G.IsNClique 3 T ∧ ∃ Y : Finset (Fin n),
          JoinedToTwo G T Y ∧ (1 / 2 - ε) * (n : ℝ) < (Y.card : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Faudree asked about the threshold $h(n)$ such that every graph with $n$ vertices and
$>n^2/4$ edges contained a triangle and $h(n)$ other vertices which are connected to at least two
vertices of the triangle. The fact that every graph with $>n^2/4$ edges contains a book of size
$n/6$ shows that
$$(1/6-o(1))n \leq h(n).$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1034.variants.lower_bound (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 4 < (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) →
        ∃ T : Finset (Fin n), G.IsNClique 3 T ∧ ∃ Y : Finset (Fin n),
          JoinedToTwo G T Y ∧ (1 / 6 - ε) * (n : ℝ) ≤ (Y.card : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
The construction of Ma and Tang [MaTa25] of a graph with $n$ vertices and $>n^2/4$ edges in which
every triangle has at most $(2-(5/2)^{1/2}+o(1))n$ vertices adjacent to at least two of its
vertices shows that, for the threshold $h(n)$ of `erdos_1034.variants.lower_bound`,
$$h(n) \leq (2-(5/2)^{1/2}+o(1))n.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1034.variants.upper_bound (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 4 < (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ∧
        ∀ T : Finset (Fin n), G.IsNClique 3 T → ∀ Y : Finset (Fin n),
          JoinedToTwo G T Y → (Y.card : ℝ) ≤ (2 - Real.sqrt (5 / 2) + ε) * (n : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős suggested that the answer is different if $G$ has no $K_4$. In the comments Ma and Tang
sketch a proof that the conjecture remains false even if we assume that $G$ contains no $K_4$,
constructing a graph with $n$ vertices, $>n^2/4$ edges, and no $K_4$, in which every triangle has
at most $(2\sqrt{3}-3+o(1))n$ vertices adjacent to at least two of its vertices (note that
$2\sqrt{3}-3\approx 0.464$).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1034.variants.k4_free (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 ∧
      (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 4 < (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ∧
        ∀ T : Finset (Fin n), G.IsNClique 3 T → ∀ Y : Finset (Fin n),
          JoinedToTwo G T Y → (Y.card : ℝ) ≤ (2 * Real.sqrt 3 - 3 + ε) * (n : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1034

reformulations.difference: The docstring and source define h(n) through 'h(n) other vertices' (vertices outside the triangle) in every G(n; ⌊n²/4⌋+1), i.e. graphs with exactly ⌊n²/4⌋+1 edges. The Lean uses `JoinedToTwo`, whose Y may contain the triangle's own vertices (each is adjacent to the other two), and quantifies over all graphs with > n²/4 edges. It also writes '(1/6 − o(1))n ≤ h(n)' as `∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ... (1/6 - ε) * n ≤ Y.card`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a fixed triangle T, the number of vertices outside T adjacent to ≥ 2 vertices of T differs from the maximal `JoinedToTwo` set by at most 3. The statement is a `∀ ε > 0, eventually in n` bound that is linear in n, so the additive constant 3 is absorbed: apply the statement with ε/2 and take n ≥ 6/ε. Also, `∃ Y, JoinedToTwo G T Y ∧ b ≤ |Y|` holds iff b ≤ |{v : v adjacent to ≥ 2 vertices of T}| (the strict analogue is proved in my scratch file). The edge conditions agree because the property is monotone. A graph with more than ⌊n²/4⌋+1 edges contains a subgraph with exactly that many. That subgraph's triangles are triangles of G, and its Y-sets are subsets of G's. So 'every graph with exactly ⌊n²/4⌋+1 edges' and 'every graph with > n²/4 edges' pose the same condition. The statement is true by the book theorem (an edge in ≥ n/6 triangles).

reformulations.difference: The docstring phrases the result as h(n) ≤ (2 − √(5/2) + o(1))n, with h(n) counting 'other' vertices in graphs with exactly ⌊n²/4⌋+1 edges. The Lean asserts, for every ε > 0 and all large n, a graph with > n²/4 edges in which every set Y of vertices joined to ≥ 2 vertices of any triangle T (T's own vertices allowed) has |Y| ≤ (2 − √(5/2) + ε)n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The Lean is exactly Ma–Tang's Theorem 2.1, which counts all vertices adjacent to ≥ 2 vertices of T, including T's own. Relative to the h(n) phrasing, the counts differ by at most 3, absorbed by ε for large n. Passing to a subgraph with exactly ⌊n²/4⌋+1 edges keeps every triangle a triangle and only shrinks the Y-sets. I proved the file's exact statement sorry-free by combining plby's `MaTang_main` (v4.33.0 version, compiled locally) with a bridging lemma over a verbatim copy of `JoinedToTwo`.

reformulations.difference: The source theorem (Quanyu Tang, forum, 27 Oct 2025) bounds Y(T) := {v ∈ V(G) \ V(T) : v has ≥ 2 neighbours in T}, which leaves out T's vertices, by (2√3 − 3 + o(1))n. The Lean bounds every `JoinedToTwo` set, which may include T's vertices, by (2√3 − 3 + ε)n for all ε > 0 and all large n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The two sets differ by at most 3 vertices, and 3 = o(n), so the two asymptotic statements are equivalent: take ε/2 and n ≥ 6/ε. Erdős's 'no K4, i.e. no vertex is joined to all three of the x's' is exactly `G.CliqueFree 4`. I also checked the claim independently. Take S independent, complete to B with |B| ≈ n/√3, and put a bipartite graph of max degree k inside B. This is K4-free, every triangle is {b1, b2, s}, and |Y(T)| ≤ |S| + 2k. Optimising gives 2√3 − 3. A numeric check gives |Y|/n = 0.4650, 0.46420, 0.464110 and 0.464102 at n = 10³ to 10⁶.

review.notes:
I found no misformalization in any of the four declarations, and no status issue.

1. `erdos_1034`: `answer(False)` elaborates to `False`, so the statement is ¬P. P is: for all ε > 0 and all sufficiently large n, every graph on `Fin n` with more than n²/4 edges has a triangle T and a set Y of more than (1/2 − ε)n vertices, each adjacent to two distinct vertices of T. This is the standard reading of erdosproblems' 't > (1/2 − o(1))n', with the threshold uniform over graphs. The polarity matches the recorded disproof. I proved P → (plby's `erdos_1034` predicate) in Lean. Combined with plby's v4.33.0 proof, which compiles here without `sorry`, this gives a complete proof of the file's exact statement using only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. So the `research solved` tag and the `formal_proof` record are consistent with erdosproblems.com ('DISPROVED (LEAN)') and teorth's database.

The linked v4.29.1 file fails on the local v4.33.1 toolchain only because of API drift (for example, `SimpleGraph.symm` is now a `Std.Symm`). It is meant for v4.29.1, so this is not a defect.

2. `upper_bound`: this is Ma–Tang's Theorem 2.1 verbatim. It is also proved sorry-free here from plby's `MaTang_main`.

3. `lower_bound`: true by the book theorem. Take an edge xy in at least n/6 triangles and T = {x, y, z₁}; then Y ⊇ the common neighbours of x and y.

4. `k4_free`: matches the forum theorem and sketch, and I checked the construction myself.

The original [Er93] paper was not available (the Rényi archive stops at 1989). Its wording ('t > n/2 − o(1)', 'h(n) other vertices') is known here through Ma–Tang §3 and the forum quotes. Erdős's literal 'n/2 − o(1)' would be a stronger conjecture than erdosproblems' '(1/2 − o(1))n'. The file follows erdosproblems, and Ma–Tang refutes both readings, so `answer(False)` is right either way.

The forum notes that finding the exact asymptotic constant of h(n) is still open. The file does not formalize that question; this is an omission, not a misformalization.
